dedupe_keys.name: eagle i recorded electricity outages by us county at 15 minute intervals 2014 2025

description: This data set gives county-level estimates of customers without electricity every 15 minutes across the United States, recorded by EAGLE-I, the Environment for Analysis of Geo-Located Energy Information, a geographic information system and visualisation platform built at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. EAGLE-I collects outage counts from the public outage maps of utilities, and the data descriptor in Scientific Data (Brelsford and co-authors) reports that by 2022 the collection represented 92 percent of customers in the 50 states, Washington DC and Puerto Rico. The Figshare record, version 4 published on 25 February 2026, now spans 2014 to 2025, with one outage file per year (the 2025 file is about 1.4 GB), a modelled count of electricity customers per county, a state coverage history and a data quality index, plus R code for the quality index and a Winter Storm Uri map. The work was supported by the DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response. Coverage is US counties, with growing utility coverage over time. Files are CSV, free to download under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: early years cover fewer utilities, counts are scraped estimates, not utility reports, and users should weight by the quality index and coverage history. Simulation uses are calibrating outage and restoration models for storms, heat and cold events and county-level resilience metrics. Related records: data-us-power-outages-county-day-corpus is a derived county-day analysis corpus.
